title: Reverse the paired DDG with a resident transcript and clean stopping counter
body:
PR6072's literal paired DDG has an exact sampling law but leaves reversible cleanup and stopping records open. This package supplies a source-bound inverse for `make(1,1)` and proves that every terminating path can copy its two-bit output, restore the resident tape cursor, and clear the DDG controller and stopping counter without storing a per-step node history.

The required boundary is explicit: phase and the consumed coin identify a unique predecessor. Dropping phase merges actual leaf transitions; stopping on a root-state revisit would also fail after a 156-step wrap. The protocol retains the transcript and counter during the call and reverses all T steps after XOR-copying the output.

The physical claim remains conditional. Forward plus cleanup uses 2T logical transitions; an explicit scan realization charges 2496T fixed-record visits plus counter, addressing and tape costs. T has no finite worst-case bound, and restoring consumed bits does not make them fresh after retaining the sampled output. No supplier, caller batching window, runtime speedup or new kappa is claimed.

Validation on Python 3.12:

- All 624 literal edges and 624 wrong-coin controls; 1,022 short terminating tapes with all four accumulator values.
- 315 terminating paths through phase wraps, up to T=314, including 316 root revisits before the counter reaches zero.
- Wrong stopping count, output, phase and cursor controls, plus a nonterminating finite prefix control.
- Registered normal/optimized replay, committed-byte/source-history preflight, official export/integrity, and identical read-only Git-free normal/optimized replay.

Exact PR6072 source bytes and predecessor credit are retained in an ancestor commit; no unmerged source-object dependency or synthetic merge is used. The 144-pair historical suite, Lean and Docker were not run. The written inverse induction supports arbitrary terminating paths; finite fixtures are implementation controls, not a formal-kernel proof.

Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. zxv's DDG source, classical method, and predecessor attribution remain intact. Follows [the task06 advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/6073#discussioncomment-19234412). Open next questions concern a fully priced physical tape/table service and an actual nonadaptive caller with conditionally fresh randomness.
